transcript: When you love yourself enough, something very quiet begins to change inside you. Not a loud confidence, not pride, not ego, but understanding. You begin to understand your needs, not the needs you were taught to ignore, not the needs you were told were too much. But the real ones, rest, safety, honesty, presence, peace. And when you truly understand them, you stop apologizing for having them. You begin to believe, softly but firmly, that your needs are worthy. Not because someone approves of them, but because they are part of your nature. And from this place, attraction changes. You no longer feel pulled toward people who cannot meet you emotionally. You no longer feel excited by inconsistency, by distance, by confusion. What once felt familiar now feels heavy. What once felt intense now feels draining. It is not that those people become bad, it is that your nervous system no longer mistakes absence for love. When you love yourself enough, you stop chasing what hurts you and start recognizing what feels like home. Not because you are stronger, but because you are finally listening. And when you listen to yourself, you naturally walk away from anything that asks you to abandon who you are. If these words slowed your breath, if something in you felt seen, you are not alone. Like this so it can reach someone who needs it today. Follow for more reflections on peace, clarity, and coming back to yourself.
